quiz.q: How do voting rules in the UN Security Council distinguish between procedural and substantive matters?
options: Procedural matters require any nine votes, while substantive matters require nine affirmative votes without a P5 veto.
Procedural matters require consensus among all members, while substantive matters require a two-thirds majority of the Council.
Procedural matters require nine votes including all P5 members, while substantive matters require only any nine votes.
Procedural matters require General Assembly approval, while substantive matters are decided exclusively by the five permanent members.
quiz.why: The notes state that procedural decisions require any nine affirmative votes, whereas substantive decisions require nine votes with no P5 veto.

quiz.q: What key procedural difference separates the G4 coalition from the Coffee Club on Security Council expansion?
options: The G4 demands immediate veto abolition, while the Coffee Club insists on extending veto to newcomers.
The G4 proposes adding only non-permanent members, while the Coffee Club seeks six new permanent seats.
The G4 advocates expansion by Article 108 majority, while the Coffee Club demands reform through full consensus.
The G4 seeks reform through the Secretariat, while the Coffee Club prefers negotiations inside the Trusteeship Council.
quiz.why: The notes highlight that G4 seeks expansion through Article 108 majority voting, whereas the Coffee Club brought the 'Uniting for Consensus' resolution demanding consensus.

quiz.q: Under Kofi Annan's UNSC reform proposals, how did Model A differ from Model B?
options: Model A granted immediate veto to newcomers, while Model B stripped existing permanent members of veto.
Model A created six new permanent seats without veto, while Model B introduced eight renewable four-year seats.
Model A was endorsed by Pakistan, while Model B received formal backing from India and the G4.
Model A expanded the Council by nine non-permanent seats, while Model B created five permanent regional seats.
quiz.why: The notes explain that Model A offered six new permanent seats without veto, whereas Model B offered eight four-year semi-permanent seats.

quiz.q: Which disputes are explicitly excluded from India's acceptance of ICJ compulsory jurisdiction under its 1974 declaration?
options: Disputes concerning maritime boundary delimitations and bilateral commercial trade disagreements governed by international treaties.
Disputes referred directly by the UN Security Council and advisory proceedings initiated by the General Assembly.
Disputes involving non-signatories of nuclear treaties and cross-border environmental damage claims occurring during peacetime.
Disputes involving Commonwealth member states and situations relating to hostilities or armed conflicts in self-defence.
quiz.why: The notes specify that India's 1974 acceptance excludes Commonwealth disputes and actions involving hostilities or armed conflicts in self-defence.
